Package com.im.njams.sdk

Class Path

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.im.njams.sdk.Path
  • public final class Path
extends Object
    Represents an immutable nJAMS path node in a shared, lazily built path tree.

    A path in nJAMS uses > as a separator and always starts and ends with it. Examples of valid path strings: >, >a>, >a>b>.

    Each instance is a unique, immutable node. The same logical path always returns the same object reference. Use of(String...) to obtain instances; there is no public constructor.

    The tree is thread-safe: reads are non-blocking; node creation is atomic per slot.

    Strict vs. resolve API — which to use

    Two parallel APIs are provided:

    • Strict (segment-based): of(String...), getChild(String...), hasChild(String...), getOrCreateChild(String...). Each argument is treated as a single segment name. Walking the tree is one ConcurrentHashMap.get per level — no parsing, no string allocation, and validation is skipped entirely for already-existing nodes.
    • Resolve (path-string-based): resolve(String...), resolveChild(String...), resolvesChild(String...), resolveOrCreateChild(String...). Each argument may be a partial path string with embedded > separators; arguments are split, empty and null segments are dropped, and the remaining segments are walked the same way as the strict variants. Split results are cached per input string, but even with a cache hit the split + cache lookup costs more than passing segments directly.

    Prefer the strict variants whenever the segment names are already known. Use the resolve variants only when the input is itself a path string — for example parsed from configuration, received from the wire, or otherwise arriving as raw text that may contain > separators.

    • Method Detail

      • of

        public static Path of​(String... segments)
        Returns the Path instance identified by the given segments.

        Calling this method with the same segments always returns the identical object. Reads are non-blocking: segment validation is skipped entirely when the child node already exists. Validation and creation are atomic per slot in the path tree.

        For arguments that may contain embedded > separators (partial path strings), use resolve(String...) instead.

        Parameters:
        segments - zero or more non-null, non-blank path segment names; must not contain >. The single value ">" is treated as the root and returns ROOT.
        Returns:
        the corresponding Path node; ROOT if no segments are provided
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if any segment is null, blank, or contains >

      • resolve

        public static Path resolve​(String... paths)
        Returns the Path instance for the given arguments, treating each argument as a (possibly partial) path string. Each argument is split at >; empty and null segments are silently dropped. The remaining segments are then walked exactly like of(String...).

        This is more lenient than of(String...): it accepts arguments such as "a>b>" or ">c>" that of would reject. Bare segment arguments such as resolve("a", "b", "c") produce the same instance as the equivalent of call.

        Split results are cached per input string to amortise the splitting overhead across repeated calls. Even with caching, this method is slower than of(String...); prefer of(String...) whenever the individual segment names are already known.

        Parameters:
        paths - zero or more path strings to split and walk; null array or null entries return / contribute nothing
        Returns:
        the resolved Path node; ROOT if no non-empty segments result
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if any resulting segment is blank or otherwise invalid

      • resolveChild

        public Path resolveChild​(String... paths)
        Returns the descendant path node reached by walking the given (possibly partial) path strings as a relative path from this node, or null if any step along the chain does not yet exist. Each argument is split at > and empty/null segments are dropped before walking.

        This is the instance counterpart of resolve(String...). Prefer getChild(String...) whenever the segment names are already known to avoid the splitting overhead.

        Parameters:
        paths - zero or more (possibly partial) path strings forming a relative path from this node; null entries are skipped
        Returns:
        the descendant path, this node if no segments result, or null if any intermediate child has not been created

      • hasChild

        public boolean hasChild​(String... names)
        Tests whether the descendant path reached by walking the given segment names exists as a chain of created children under this path. This is the strict variant: each argument is treated as a single segment name and is not parsed.

        With no arguments (or a null array) returns true (the empty relative path always exists). A null entry in the array returns false (a null segment cannot identify a child).

        For arguments that may contain embedded > separators (partial path strings), use resolvesChild(String...) instead — it splits each argument and drops empty/null segments, at the cost of splitting overhead.

        Parameters:
        names - zero or more segment names forming a relative path from this node
        Returns:
        true if the full chain has been created; false otherwise
        See Also:
        resolvesChild(String...)

      • resolvesChild

        public boolean resolvesChild​(String... paths)
        Tests whether the descendant path reached by walking the given (possibly partial) path strings exists as a chain of created children under this path. Each argument is split at > and empty segments are dropped before walking; null entries in the array are silently skipped.

        With no arguments (or a null array) returns true (the empty relative path always exists).

        This is the lenient counterpart of hasChild(String...): it accepts arguments such as "a>b>" or ">c>" that hasChild would treat as a single (and therefore non-matching) segment. Prefer hasChild(String...) when the segment names are already known, to avoid the splitting overhead.

        Parameters:
        paths - zero or more (possibly partial) path strings forming a relative path from this node; null entries are skipped
        Returns:
        true if the full chain has been created; false otherwise
        See Also:
        hasChild(String...)

        This is the instance counterpart of resolve(String...). Prefer getOrCreateChild(String...) whenever the segment names are already known to avoid the splitting overhead.

        Returns the descendant path node reached by walking the given segment names as a relative path from this node, creating any missing intermediate children along the way. Concurrent calls with the same names return the identical instance for each level.

      • startsWith

        public boolean startsWith​(Path prefix)
        Returns true if this path is the given prefix itself or a descendant of it.

        Because paths are unique singleton nodes, the test walks the parent chain up to the prefix's depth and compares by identity; it allocates nothing. ROOT is a prefix of every path, and every path is a prefix of itself. A prefix deeper than this path can never be an ancestor, so the depth check fails fast without any walking.

        Parameters:
        prefix - the candidate ancestor path; null returns false
        Returns:
        true if this path starts with prefix

      • print

        public static String print​(Path root)
        Returns an ASCII-art rendering of the path subtree rooted at the given node, one line per node and with children sorted by segment name for stable output. Intended for diagnostics and debugging; pass ROOT to render the entire tree.

        Example for a node root with children a (containing b and c) and d: 

         root
 +- a
 |  +- b
 |  `- c
 `- d
        Parameters:
        root - the subtree root to render; null yields an empty string
        Returns:
        a multi-line ASCII representation of the subtree, terminated by a newline per node; an empty string if root is null
